_: The core user units, one row each. THE only list: install.sh links and enables from it, cc-audit checks health from it, cc-land reads its restart policy from it, and tests/check.sh fails when a unit file and this file disagree. Adding a timer = its two unit files + one row here.

_fields.enable: required = install.sh enables it and cc-audit FAILS when it is not enabled · owner = linked only, the box owner switches it on, and cc-audit checks its health only once they have · timer = started by its own .timer, never enabled and never health-checked
_fields.start: what install.sh does after enabling: now = --now · no-block = start --no-block (a oneshot that may wait minutes for the network must never block the installer) · none
_fields.health: active = systemctl is-active must say active · not-failed = a oneshot that has run and gone idle, only is-failed is a fault · none
_fields.restart: what a landing does when this unit's file, or a file its ExecStart runs, changes: restart = restart it · rearm = restart it AND confirm list-timers shows a next trigger (daemon-reload alone leaves a changed OnCalendar with Trigger: n/a — a daily job silently switched off, 2026-08-31) · owner = never automatically, the landing records the owner action instead · none = nothing to restart, the next start picks the change up

units.why: owns the shared tmux server every session on this box lives in — restarting it takes all of them down, so it is the owner's hand (`cc rc restart`)
the 10 s alive timestamp that dates a power loss
a boot oneshot: restarting it would re-announce a boot that already happened
the 60 s model-fallback tick: switched off, a usage limit stops every loop on the box
the weekly sweep of dead tracks, merged origin branches and bare windows — enabled everywhere because a box with no CC_JANITOR_REPOS sweeps nothing

the drive loop — every 2 h it wakes each session so one decides whether there is work; switched off, the box does nothing until a human asks. INSTALLED OFF: the first run wakes every session on this box at once, and switching that on is the owner's call, not the installer's
enabled even when publishing is unconfigured — it exits at once, and after a later `cc-publish setup` it must not wait for a second install
`cc slack on` owns it — it needs the tokens, so the installer never starts it
an always-on recorder is the box owner's call
